clinician.final_diagnosis: Dermatophytosis and keratomycosis caused by Trichophyton interdigitale with loss of vision in the left eye
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man presented with a 4-year history of progressive dermatophytosis that began near the left eyebrow and extended to face, trunk, and limbs, complicated by onychomycosis of the left hand and fungal keratitis leading to vision loss in the left eye. Initial workup on admission revealed hyaline septate hyphae on KOH microscopy (E002). Culture of biopsy specimens from skin lesions, nail clippings, and corneal scrapings grew white downy colonies on Sabouraud dextrose agar (E002). Molecular identification by ITS sequencing confirmed 99% identity with T. interdigitale (E003). Histopathological examination of skin biopsy showed parakeratosis, mild acanthosis, dense dermal vascularization, and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration consistent with dermatophyte infection (E004). Following diagnosis, the patient was treated with luliconazole cream twice daily and oral itraconazole 100mg BID for one month, with significant clinical improvement observed after 14 days (E008). The patient subsequently underwent enucleation of the left eye due to the severe keratomycosis, and remained without recurrence at 3-month follow-up (E008).
